explanation: Compare entries in pairs. Only the smaller needs comparison with the minimum, and only the larger with the maximum. Initialize with one entry for odd lengths or the first pair for even lengths.
timeComplexity: O(n), using at most ceil(3n/2) - 2 value comparisons. Each pair costs three comparisons, with a constant-size singleton/odd-tail adjustment.
spaceComplexity: O(1). Only current pair extrema and global extrema are retained.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: After each processed pair, minimum and maximum are the extrema of all processed entries. Comparing the two new entries first determines which alone can lower minimum and which alone can raise maximum. Three comparisons per pair preserve the invariant; one initial entry or pair establishes it.
walkthrough: For [7,-3,12,4,0], initialize both extrema to 7. The pair (-3,12) changes them to (-3,12). The pair (4,0) has local extrema (0,4), neither improving the global extrema. Return (-3,12).
edgeCases: One entry is both the minimum and maximum.
Odd length initializes from one entry; even length initializes from a pair.
Equal entries require no special handling.
